goals: Handle work talk and polite requests

lessons.title: Stories: pretérito vs imperfecto
lessons.learn: Two pasts! PRETÉRITO = finished actions (LLEGUÉ = I arrived). IMPERFECTO = ongoing scenes (HACÍA SOL = the sun was shining). Tell stories: set the scene with imperfecto, fire events with pretérito.

grammar.title: Pretérito vs imperfecto: hablé vs hablaba
grammar.explain: HABLÉ = I spoke (done). HABLABA = I was speaking / used to speak (ongoing). -AR imperfecto: HABLABA, HABLABAS, HABLABA. Weather, feelings, habits → imperfecto. Single events → pretérito.

examples.en: I was speaking when you arrived.

mistakes: Using pretérito for weather: HACÍA sol, not HIZO sol.
Using imperfecto for single arrivals: LLEGUÉ, not LLEGABA.

dialogue.en: It was big. There was music and we danced.

lessons.title: Opinions and comparisons
lessons.learn: Compare with MÁS…QUE (more…than) and MENOS…QUE (less…than). Specials: MEJOR (better), PEOR (worse). Give opinions: CREO QUE (I think that), EN MI OPINIÓN (in my opinion).

grammar.title: Comparisons: más… que, mejor, peor
grammar.explain: MÁS + adjective + QUE = more…than: MÁS GRANDE QUE = bigger than. EL MÁS… = the most: EL MÁS GRANDE = the biggest. MEJOR and PEOR never take MÁS — MEJOR already means better!

examples.t: Es más grande que mi casa.
examples.r: ehs mahs GRAHN-deh keh mee KAH-sah.
examples.en: It is bigger than my house.

mistakes: Saying MÁS MEJOR — just MEJOR (better already!).
Forgetting QUE: MÁS GRANDE QUE, with QUE!

lessons.title: Contar una anécdota: primero, luego, de repente
lessons.learn: Spanish anecdotes mix the pretérito for events and the imperfecto for the scene: PRIMERO LLEGAMOS, LUEGO EMPEZÓ A LLOVER, DE REPENTE SE FUE LA LUZ. The imperfect describes; the preterite acts.

grammar.title: Scene and event
grammar.pattern: imperfecto for the background · pretérito for the event · time adverbs fronted
grammar.explain: Estábamos en casa, llovía y de repente se fue la luz. The scene is imperfect, the turn is preterite — that pairing is what makes a Spanish story sound native.

examples.en: First we arrived at the hotel.

examples.t: Llovía y de repente se fue la luz.
examples.r: yoh-VEE-ah ee deh reh-PEN-teh seh fweh lah looz.
examples.en: It was raining and suddenly the power went out.
In the end everything turned out well.

mistakes.why: de repente introduces an event: preterite.

mistakes.wrong: Estuvimos en casa y llovió toda la tarde. (scene)

dialogue.en: What happened yesterday?

dialogue.t: Estábamos en el bar, hablábamos tranquilamente y de repente se fue la luz.
dialogue.r: es-TAH-bah-mohs en el bar, ah-BLAH-bah-mohs trahn-kee-lah-MEN-teh ee deh reh-PEN-teh seh fweh lah looz.
dialogue.en: We were in the bar, talking quietly, and suddenly the power went out.
And then?

dialogue.t: Luego todos sacamos el móvil y seguimos hablando igual.
dialogue.r: LWEH-goh TOH-dohs sah-KAH-mohs el MOH-veel ee seh-GEE-mohs ah-BLAN-doh ee-GWAL.
dialogue.en: Then we all took out our phones and kept talking anyway.

lessons.title: Work and polite YOU (usted)
lessons.learn: At work, use USTED (polite you) with strangers and bosses. Usted uses HE/SHE verb forms: ¿HABLA inglés? = Do you (formal) speak English? TÚ is for friends; USTED is for respect.

grammar.title: USTED: polite you uses he/she forms
grammar.explain: ¿HABLAS? (tú, friend) vs ¿HABLA? (usted, formal). Same -A ending as HE/SHE. Use usted with bosses, elders, officials. Dropping it too fast can sound rude!
mistakes: Using TÚ with a new boss — start with USTED.
Using HABLAS with usted — usted takes HABLA.

lessons.title: Plans and wishes
lessons.learn: Dream big! QUISIERA (I would like) + verb makes soft wishes: QUISIERA VIAJAR = I would like to travel. QUIZÁ (maybe) + future guesses: QUIZÁ VIAJARÉ = maybe I will travel. OJALÁ (hopefully!) opens every dream.

grammar.title: Soft wishes: quisiera + verb
grammar.explain: QUISIERA = I would like. Add any verb whole: QUISIERA APRENDER = I would like to learn. QUIZÁ (maybe) softens guesses. These two words make you sound kind and natural.
mistakes: Changing the verb after QUISIERA: QUISIERA VIAJAR, verb stays whole.
Saying QUIERO for soft wishes — QUISIERA is kinder.

lessons.title: Buscar trabajo: currículum, entrevista, usted
lessons.learn: Applications and interviews keep the usted register: ¿POR QUÉ SE INTERESA POR ESTE PUESTO? · TENGO EXPERIENCIA EN … The polite forms are usted forms, not third-person accidents.

grammar.title: Interview register
grammar.pattern: ¿por qué se interesa por…? · tengo experiencia en … · me gustaría …

lessons.title: Future tense: viajaré
lessons.learn: The real future adds endings to the WHOLE verb: VIAJAR → VIAJARÉ (I will travel), VIAJARÁS (you will), VIAJARÁ (he/she will). Never changes the stem — just add -É/-ÁS/-Á!

grammar.title: Future: whole verb + é/ás/á
grammar.explain: Keep the infinitive, add -É, -ÁS, -Á: HABLARÉ, COMERÉ, VIVIRÉ. Works for -AR, -ER, -IR — all the same! A few rebels (TENDRÉ, HARÉ) come later.
mistakes: Cutting the verb: VIAJARÉ keeps -AR + É — never VIAJÉ for future!
Confusing VIAJÉ (past I) with VIAJARÉ (future I).

lessons.title: TV, news, and LO/LA (it)
lessons.learn: Replace things with LO (him/it-masculine) and LA (her/it-feminine): VEO LA PELÍCULA → LA VEO (I see it). LO/LA jump BEFORE the verb. News words: NOTICIAS, PROGRAMA, PELÍCULA.

grammar.title: LO/LA: it jumps before the verb
grammar.explain: Veo el programa → LO veo (I see it). Veo la película → LA veo. LO = masculine IT, LA = feminine IT. Always before the verb: LO sé = I know it.

mistakes: Saying VEO LO — LO must jump before: LO veo.

items.q: Say: I would like to travel
Say aloud: Quisiera viajar a España.

culture.text: The Spanish working day still bends around the middle of the day: a long lunch, often at home, and business that runs into the evening. The siesta is not laziness but the shape of a climate and a timetable; in the cities it has shrunk to a short pause, while the evening meeting and the late dinner remain. B1 needs the vocabulary because work is the first place a learner is asked about plans in a register that is neither home nor classroom.

reading.text: Ana trabaja en una oficina en Sevilla. «Entro a las ocho y salgo a las tres», dice. «Luego como en casa y duermo veinte minutos.» Por la tarde vuelve al trabajo si hay una reunión con clientes de América: «A las siete hablamos con México, así que la tarde es larga.» Después cursa una formación: «Quiero cambiar de departamento el año que viene.»
reading.gloss: Ana works in an office in Seville. 'I start at eight and leave at three,' she says. 'Then I eat at home and sleep twenty minutes.' In the afternoon she goes back to work if there is a meeting with clients from America: 'At seven we talk to Mexico, so the afternoon is long.' Afterwards she takes a training course: 'I want to change department next year.'

mistakes.wrong: Tengo 25 años y trabajo aquí desde tres años.
mistakes.right: Tengo 25 años y trabajo aquí desde hace tres años.
mistakes.why: Duration takes desde hace; desde alone marks a point in time.

mistakes.wrong: Estoy de acuerdo contigo, pero pienso que no es posible el plan.
mistakes.right: … pero creo que el plan no es posible.
mistakes.why: Spanish prefers the negative before the verb and the subject after it.

mistakes.right: Mañana iré a trabajar y después comeré.
mistakes.why: Pronouns are dropped when the verb ending already carries the person.

task.title: Describe your working life in ninety seconds
task.instructions: Record ninety seconds in Spanish about what you do and what comes next: current job or study, one thing that was hard at the start, one plan for next year. Use one «desde hace», one «para que + subjunctive» and one reflexive verb. Listen back and count the sentences where the verb ending and the subject disagree — those are the ones to rewrite.
